source_inspection_only: Traced reserve recovery against ReconcilePublicControlSlots and the existing Charge migration rule. The mixed legacy bar in R8-F1 is absent from the reserve recovery regression.
Traced native invalidation through MountedControlPlacementIntent.Reconcile for a faulted rider. The toolbar double derives eligibility solely from a resolving pet, so it cannot exercise R8-F2.

findings.actual: AdmitReserveBindings takes the first index matching either a legacy alias or the public control. A legacy Mount at 3 therefore wins over the player's public control at 9. It then calls ClearManagedHotbarSlots, which also erases a legacy Mounted Charge at 5 without applying the stock Charge migration. An immediate city resave makes both changes persistent.
findings.blocking_rationale: The newly added recovery path can permanently move the reported shortcut and delete another recoverable shortcut in a supported older save.
findings.expected: As in ReconcilePublicControlSlots, an existing public Mount / Dismount binding wins over a legacy Mount or Dismount alias. A legacy Mounted Charge becomes the rider's stock Charge at the same index when stock Charge is available and absent elsewhere on the bar.
findings.requested_correction: Apply the existing migration precedence before clearing reserve bindings. Recover the canonical public slot first, fall back to an exact legacy Mount or Dismount when needed, and preserve the existing stock Charge migration and duplicate rule.
findings.requested_evidence: Start an unobserved reserve rider with legacy Mount at 3, legacy Mounted Charge at 5, public Mount / Dismount at 9, an available stock Charge fact and no owned rows. Save immediately and reload. Verify one kind-6 row at 9, stock Charge at 5, no native KMC binding during serialization, and one public control at 9 on return. Repeat with stock Charge already bound elsewhere and verify it stays there once.
findings.title: Older reserve bars bypass the existing shortcut migration rules
findings.trigger: The first update or save scans an older capital save whose reserve rider still has legacy KMC bindings on the native bar.

findings.actual: The invalidation observer preserves the interrupted index because ShouldLease is true. On the next update, Reconcile reaches the live, unbound branch and calls Revalidate unconditionally. Revalidate retires the entry for an empty pet ID. ResolveUnbound then records an already-placed rider as off-bar, losing the index.
findings.blocking_rationale: Native cleanup can remove the player's Dismount shortcut precisely while the relationship still provides it as an escape from a faulted state.
findings.expected: An interrupted slot returns to its chosen empty index while the relationship still grants the public control. A confirmed companion replacement, or a cleared link after entitlement ends, still retires it.
findings.requested_correction: Use the same entitlement-aware companion-loss decision in live unbound reconciliation as in the invalidation observer. Preserve the known companion identity and interrupted index while the relationship grants the control.
findings.requested_evidence: Record slot 9 for pet A, clear the pet link while the mounted or faulted relationship still grants Dismount, then invalidate the bound slot and reconcile the live control. Verify exactly one binding and one saved kind-6 row at 9. Keep the dismounted cleared-link and different-pet controls passing.
findings.title: A faulted rider loses an interrupted shortcut while Dismount is still available
findings.trigger: Native bad-slot cleanup empties the chosen slot while the rider's pet link is empty and NativeMountedControlPolicy.ShouldLease still grants MountState through the mounted or faulted relationship.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: Boundary observation now retires a dismounted rider's arrangement before a cleared link can overwrite its known companion identity. In-world seeding and slot replay honor that retirement. The gate covers replacement before resume, both replay orderings, and restoration for the unchanged pet ID.

The reserve scan reaches a never-observed rider at the save header and before serialization. For the reported single binding at 9, the focused case confirms one kind-6 row, one placement record, zero serialized KMC slots, one restoration on return and disable cleanup. R8-F1 concerns how the new scan handles additional legacy bindings.

The city issues share a roster transition as a trigger. Toolbar fact loss and the native UI pet filter are distinct causes.
